source.title: Gradient Diversity: a Key Ingredient for Scalable Distributed Learning
source.authors: Dong Yin; A. Pananjady; Maximilian Lam; Dimitris Papailiopoulos; K. Ramchandran; P. Bartlett

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. No apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how minibatch size affects generalization behavior and reports CIFAR-10 experiments, using stability and generalization measures rather than the original large-batch generalization-gap setup.
record.gate_note: The main experimental generalization results are Figure 4b–c, but the text describes higher variance in generalization behavior without giving numerical train/test errors or explicit error-gap values. Those findings bear on V5 as a stated effect, but do not quantify its direction or size. Figure 4a measures model distance, not the generalization gap, so it is not a row. The paper's citations to prior large-batch work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Section 6.2 and Figures 4b–c compare training error, test error and their absolute difference across data passes for CIFAR-10 convolutional networks with batches 512 and 1024. These measures bear on V5. However, the supplied text preserves no readable curve values, and the reported higher variance does not establish worse held-out performance at matched epoch budgets.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but overstates the theoretical guarantee as matching actual generalization. The authors establish comparable generalization-error upper bounds under convex or strongly convex assumptions and suitable batch-size and step-size conditions. Their CIFAR-10 experiments report reduced parameter stability and higher variance in generalization behavior with larger batches.
record.recipe_differences: Studies minibatch SGD and stability/generalization under varying batch sizes; it does not reproduce the cited large-batch generalization-gap method.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes model stability and the reported variance in generalization behavior; the text compares B=512 and B=1024.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized parameter distance between models trained on datasets differing by one example increases with batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger batches can reduce parameter stability in CIFAR-10 convolutional-network training.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report higher variance in generalization behavior for larger batches without stating a directional held-out-error comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects variability in generalization behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Under convexity, smoothness, step-size and differential-gradient-diversity assumptions, minibatch SGD has generalization-error upper bounds comparable to serial SGD at equal gradient-update counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Differential gradient diversity permits comparable generalization-gap guarantees for serial and minibatch SGD under specified assumptions.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The relevant generalization experiment is presented as plots; the prose reports higher variance but provides no numerical train/test error or gap values. Results are averaged over 3 experiments. The experiment concerns one CIFAR-10 cuda convolutional network setup.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4a's normalized distance between models trained on datasets differing by one point is a stability measure, not a measure named by the claim versions. Figures 4b–c are discussed qualitatively but lack numeric results in the text, so no row can be assigned under the row rules.

Language models and the effects of longer training, warmup, learning-rate scaling, normalization or regularization changes on held-out performance. The direction of the matched-epoch test-error comparison cannot be determined from the supplied figure text.
Dropout's effect on held-out error; the dropout experiments measure training-loss convergence.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is justified by the available directional evidence. Comparable upper bounds do not establish equal realized held-out performance, and increased variance does not establish V5's penalty. Figures 4b–c are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not added to missing. Numeric values are not required for qualitative rows, but the supplied prose cannot determine V5's effect state.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.

The CIFAR-10 experiment compares generalization behavior at batch sizes 512 and 1024, but the text gives no separately assignable numeric error or gap values; figures show the curves without stated numbers. Other listed adaptations are not tested.
Dropout is discussed as a gradient-diversity mechanism and in convergence experiments, but no dropout result on held-out error is reported.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
